title: Query failed
intro: The RAG chatbot answers 'query failed' to every content question. You asked for tests at three layers before any fix. Open the results and locate the break.

facts.label: The symptom
facts.value: Every content-related question returns 'query failed'. Outline questions (different tool) still work fine.

facts.label: Layer 1 — the search tool
facts.value: Tests on CourseSearchTool.execute: the tool runs without errors but returns zero results for queries that should obviously match.

facts.label: Layer 2 — the AI generator
facts.value: Tests confirm ai_generator.py correctly requests the CourseSearchTool with sensible parameters. The call chain is healthy.

facts.label: Layer 3 — the RAG system
facts.value: End-to-end tests show the system handles the empty result set by reporting failure — the error message is downstream of an empty search.

question: What's broken?
choices: The AI generator calls the wrong tool
MAX_RESULTS is 0 — the search is asked to return nothing, and every layer above faithfully handles an empty result
The vector database has lost its collections
The chatbot's error handling is too aggressive
debrief: The layered tests did exactly what they were designed to do: layer 2 exonerated the call chain, layer 3 showed the failure message was honest handling of an empty set, and layer 1 pinned the anomaly — a healthy tool returning nothing. That triangulation points at configuration, and there it is: MAX_RESULTS = 0, a search told to return zero results. The method is the lesson: 'fix the query failure' invites a plausible patch to the wrong layer; tests at three altitudes force the failure to localize itself before anyone proposes a fix.
